description: Small synthetic golden set for the offline CI eval. Labels stand in for an analyst. Narratives use documentation addresses only.

cases.label: true_positive
cases.narrative: User 1001 at tenant-a failed login 40 times in ten minutes from 203.0.113.10. No later success from that address.

scripted_investigator.rationale: The failure burst has no later successful sign-in from that documentation address.

cases.label: true_positive
cases.narrative: Host host-1001 at tenant-a uploaded 2 GB to 203.0.113.20 outside the usual transfer window.

scripted_investigator.rationale: The upload size and destination are far outside this host's usual pattern.

cases.label: true_positive
cases.narrative: User 1001 disabled audit logging on tenant-a for project example-app from 203.0.113.30.

scripted_investigator.rationale: Audit logging was turned off from an address this user has not used before.

cases.label: true_positive
cases.narrative: Account 1001 at tenant-a requested 25 one-time codes in three minutes from 198.51.100.10, then none were used.

scripted_investigator.rationale: The code requests were unused and came from a new network for this account.

cases.label: false_positive
cases.narrative: The tenant-a backup job ran at 07:00 from 192.0.2.10, matching its daily schedule.

scripted_investigator.rationale: This is the documented daily backup from its usual address.

cases.label: false_positive
cases.narrative: User 1001 signed in to example.com from 192.0.2.20 during business hours on a known device.

scripted_investigator.rationale: Known device, usual hour, and a documentation address.

cases.label: false_positive
cases.narrative: User 1001 changed a firewall rule on tenant-a during the published Tuesday change window.

scripted_investigator.rationale: The change matches the published window and the operator's usual admin work.

cases.label: false_positive
cases.narrative: Service account svc-reader called the tenant-a inventory API from 192.0.2.30 at the usual minute.

scripted_investigator.rationale: The caller, path, and schedule match the usual inventory sync.
